land.text: the East Frankish kingdom of the Carolingians; in 911 the nobles of Saxony, Franconia, Bavaria and Swabia 'no longer followed the tradition' of choosing a Carolingian and chose Conrad I

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's East Franks row ends 910 and this row begins 911. The Kingdom of Germany page says the kingdom 'evolved from the eastern Frankish kingdom formed by the Treaty of Verdun in 843', so the two rows are one realm.

land.text: the whole realm of Otto I, German lands and, from late 961, Italy, passes into the Empire on his coronation at Rome

successors.note: Not a conquest: 'From 962, the kings of Germany claimed the imperial title' (Kingdom of Germany page). Cliopatria draws the Empire as a new row from 962; the colour and family agents should decide whether it is the same state under a new title.

capitals.name: Frankfurt (itinerant court; Regensburg also named)
capitals.note: East Francia infobox: capital 'Various, including Frankfurt and Ratisbon (Regensburg)'; the page gives no years. The kings moved between palaces; Otto I was crowned at Aachen (7 August 936, Otto I page).

rulers.name: Conrad I (Conrad the Younger)
rulers.note: Elected 10 November 911 (East Francia page); died 23 December 918 (Henry the Fowler page).

rulers.name: Henry I the Fowler
rulers.note: King 'from about 24 May 919 to 2 July 936' (infobox); 'elected and crowned king in 919'.

rulers.name: Otto I the Great
rulers.note: Crowned at Aachen 7 August 936; crowned Emperor at Rome in early February 962 and king until 973, the later years being the Holy Roman Empire's dossier.

keyframe_review.note: 308,194 km2 for 911-921. 'In 911 Saxon, Franconian, Bavarian and Swabian nobles' ended the Carolingian choice of king and 'on 10 November 911 elected one of their own', Conrad I (East Francia page); the Lotharingia page says in 911 'Lotharingian nobles under the new duke Reginar voted to attach their duchy to West Francia', which is why the shape stops short of the Meuse and Rhine lands. Measured on the gazetteer grid the shape covers all of Franconia (151 of 151 cells), nearly all of Bavaria (284/287), Swabia (228/229) and Thuringia (70/73) and only 1 cell of modern Sachsen: the Slav lands beyond the Elbe and Saale are out. No page opened gives an area, so the infobox comparison cannot be made (East Francia page: no area). Bavaria under Arnulf did not submit until 921 (ledger).

307,423 km2 for 922-925, the same limits as 911-921 (a few Alpine cells differ). Lotharingia stays outside until 925: it is still in West Francia's hands, Henry 'invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)' only in 923 and the Lotharingians 'elected Henry the Fowler to be their king' in 925 (Lotharingia page). The 923-925 fighting is the ledger's contest_start/contest_end.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 926 shape unchanged, valid for 926-927 only; from 928 the new keyframes apply

keyframe_review.note: 427,059 km2: adds Lotharingia (536 cells, all inside Cliopatria's West Franks shape of 925) and loses a strip from Basel to Zurich (17 cells) to Upper Burgundy. 'In 925 Lotharingia was finally ceded to East Francia by Rudolph of West Francia' (Kingdom of Germany page); the Basel estates went to Rudolph II of Burgundy for the Holy Lance 'in 926 or 935' (Rudolph II page). The shape is right for 926-927 only; the conquests Henry made in the east in 928 and 934 are in the two new keyframes that follow, which run to 935. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 926..927 from this entry's own 'valid for 926-927 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 926 shape with the Hevelli country round Brandenburg and the Gana (Jahna) district by Meissen, both taken in the campaigns of 928-929

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 928-933: the 926 shape plus the Hevelli capital Brandenburg and the Slav stronghold Gana (Jahna) near Meissen. 'In the winter of 928 he marched against the Slavic Hevelli tribes' and took Brandenburg; Henry conquered 'the capital Gana (Jahna) after a siege' (Henry the Fowler page). The page gives the strongholds, not a frontier, so the two circles are the researcher's reading; Cliopatria draws the whole Elbe-Saale country only from 936.

correction.text: the 928 keyframe with Schleswig, conquered in 934

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 934-935: as 928-933 plus Schleswig. Henry 'also conquered Schleswig in 934' (Henry the Fowler page). The page gives neither the extent of the Mark nor when it was lost; Cliopatria's Danish rows hold Schleswig from 936, so the circle at Hedeby is drawn for 934-935 only (ledger loss 936 at confidence 1).

476,221 km2: +221 cells (about 56,000 km2) over the 926 shape, nearly all in Brandenburg (102), Sachsen-Anhalt (50) and Sachsen (48) with 8 in Mecklenburg, only 8 cells of it in any other Cliopatria polity in 935 (so land of Slav tribes, 'nobody'). It matches the page's two marches: in 936 Otto 'appointed Hermann Billung as Margrave' of a march north of the Elbe and in 937 Gero succeeded his brother Siegfried as margrave of the border region around Merseburg (Otto I page). The page dates the appointments, not the frontier; Cliopatria's 936 is a year early for Gero. After 939 Otto 'assumed direct rule over the Duchy of Franconia' (internal, no border change).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 947 shape unchanged for 947-951, with the Obotrite share (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and east Holstein) drawn as vassal land, not direct territory

keyframe_review.note: 518,771 km2 for 947-959: +182 cells over 940, of which 65 lie on the land of Cliopatria's Obotrites, whose row ends 946 (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 74, Brandenburg 27, Sachsen 25, Poland 28, Schleswig-Holstein 24). No page opened dates a conquest in 946-947; the Otto I page has Hermann Billung fighting 'the Lutici, Obotrites, and Wagri' without a year and the Obotrites invading Saxony in the fall of 955, so the Obotrite land was not yet integrated: it is a tributary zone (direct to vassal), the rest is Gero's march. Shape unchanged, valid for 947-951; from 952 the next keyframe adds the March of Verona.

union.text: the March of Verona: the Duchy of Friuli reorganised under Henry of Bavaria, with Verona

correction.text: the 947 shape plus the March of Verona, Friuli reorganised under Henry of Bavaria in August 952

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 952-959: the 947 shape plus the March of Verona. At Augsburg in August 952 Berengar II 'cede[d] the Duchy of Friuli'; 'Friuli was reorganized as the March of Verona and placed under Henry's control' (Otto I page); the Kingdom of Germany page adds that the March of Verona was 'annexed by Duchy of Bavaria in 952'. Cliopatria never draws Friuli as German before 961.

union.text: the March of Verona: the Duchy of Friuli reorganised under Henry of Bavaria, with Verona

correction.text: Cliopatria's 960 shape plus the March of Verona

keyframe_review.note: 576,342 km2 in the single year 960: +229 cells in Austria (169), Slovenia (58) and Carinthia (22), 179 of them inside Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary shape of 955. The Otto I page says only that the Lechfeld victory of 10 August 955 ended 'nearly 100 years of Hungarian invasions' and does not describe any march in Pannonia, so the growth is Cliopatria's and unverified here (ledger gain at confidence 1). The March of Verona (Friuli) is added from 952.

736,897 km2: +623 cells, all of them Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy shape of 961, which Otto took in his second expedition ('descended into northern Italy in August 961 through the Brenner Pass'; 'assumed the title King of Italy at Pavia around Christmas'). The shape is held to Otto's imperial coronation of early February 962 (end of this dossier); the lands then belong to the Empire (holy-roman-empire dossier). Italy was a vassal kingdom from August 952 to December 961 (ledger) and the shape shows it whole for all of 961.

region.text: the four stem duchies that elected Conrad I (Saxony with Thuringia, Franconia, Bavaria, Swabia)

ledger.note: 911: the nobles of Saxony, Franconia, Bavaria and Swabia elect Conrad I king of the East Franks. 'on 10 November 911 elected one of their own' (East Francia page); Thuringia 'had been absorbed into Saxony in 908' (Kingdom of Germany page).

919: the crown passes from the Franconian Conrad I to the Saxon Henry the Fowler, founder of the Ottonian line. 'On 23 December 918 Conrad I ... died'; 'Henry was elected and crowned king in 919'; infobox reign 'about 24 May 919' to 2 July 936 (Henry the Fowler page). The Kingdom of Germany page says Henry's election was regarded as marking the kingdom's beginning, though Otto of Freising disagreed.

region.text: Arnulf's Bavaria, defiant of the crown until 921

ledger.note: 921: Henry marches against Duke Arnulf of Bavaria, who had taken the royal title. 'He would not submit until Henry defeated him in two campaigns in 921' (Henry the Fowler page). Conrad I's earlier struggle with Arnulf had cost him his life (East Francia page).

region.text: Arnulf's Bavaria

ledger.note: 921: Arnulf of Bavaria renounces the crown and submits to Henry. '[Arnulf] in 921 renounced the crown and submitted to Henry' (Henry the Fowler page); the same year, on 7 November, Henry and Charles the Simple conclude the Treaty of Bonn.

region.text: Lotharingia including Alsace, in West Francia's hands since 911

ledger.note: 923: Henry the Fowler invades Lotharingia, then held for West Francia. 'king Henry the Fowler of East Francia used this opportunity and invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)' (Lotharingia page). In 911 the Lotharingian nobles had attached the duchy to West Francia.

region.text: Lotharingia including Alsace

ledger.note: 925: the fighting for Lotharingia ends in Henry's favour. 'in 925 Lotharingia was finally ceded to East Francia by Rudolph of West Francia' (Kingdom of Germany page); 'In 925, Lotharingians under Gilbert elected Henry the Fowler to be their king' (Lotharingia page).

region.text: Lotharingia, the Rhineland west of the Rhine, the Low Countries and Alsace as the Duchy of Lorraine

ledger.note: 925: Lotharingia passes to the German king. 'in 925 Lotharingia was finally ceded to East Francia by Rudolph of West Francia' and 'formed the Duchy of Lorraine within the East Frankish kingdom' (Kingdom of Germany page). In 925 Duke Gilbert also rebelled and Henry besieged him and mastered much of his lands; Henry married his daughter Gerberga to Gilbert in 928 (Henry the Fowler page).

region.text: the Swabian estates round Basel and Zurich, a strip of 17 cells taken out of the 925 shape

ledger.note: 926: the Basel estates go to Burgundy for the Holy Lance. 'In 926 or 935, Rudolph rendered the royal symbol of the Holy Lance to the East Frankish king Henry the Fowler' in exchange for 'the Swabian Basel estates' (Rudolph II of Burgundy page: the page gives 926 or 935 and does not say clearly which party got the lands; Cliopatria draws the loss in 926).

region.text: the Hevelli country round their capital Brandenburg

ledger.note: 928: Henry takes Brandenburg from the Hevelli. 'In the winter of 928 he marched against the Slavic Hevelli tribes' and took their capital, Brandenburg (Henry the Fowler page).

region.text: the Gana (Jahna) district on the Elbe by Meissen

ledger.note: 928-929: Henry conquers the Slav stronghold of Gana (Jahna) in the winter campaign. Henry conquered 'the capital Gana (Jahna) after a siege' (Henry the Fowler page); the extract of the page puts it in the same campaign as the Hevelli. Counts Bernard and Thietmar rout the Redarii at Lenzen on 4 September 929 (war entry).

region.text: the Duchy of Bohemia

ledger.note: 929: Duke Wenceslaus of Bohemia is forced to pay tribute again. 'In 929, with the help of Arnulf of Bavaria, Henry entered the Duchy of Bohemia' and 'forced Duke Wenceslaus I to resume the annual payment of tribute' (Henry the Fowler page).

region.text: Schleswig, the Danish border town of Hedeby and its surroundings

ledger.note: 934: Henry conquers Schleswig from the Danes. Henry 'also conquered Schleswig in 934' (Henry the Fowler page). The page gives no extent for it.

region.text: Schleswig round Hedeby

ledger.note: 936: the Danes hold Schleswig again in Cliopatria. The page is silent on when the Mark of Schleswig was lost; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Denmark row begins in 936 and holds Schleswig, so this is a bridging date for the researcher's own reading, not a page's.

region.text: the Duchy of Bohemia

ledger.note: 936: Boleslaus of Bohemia breaks with the Saxons. 'Boleslaus attacked an ally of the Saxons in northwest Bohemia in 936' (Otto I page); the page does not say that the tribute stopped, which is the reading from the attack and the war that ran to 950.

region.text: Bohemia, with the first fighting in the northwest

ledger.note: 936: the Bohemian war begins. 'Boleslaus attacked an ally of the Saxons in northwest Bohemia in 936'; 'The war was not concluded until 950' (Otto I page). The page names northwest Bohemia as the first fighting; the contested zone drawn is the duchy, a reading.

region.text: the Elbe-Saale and Havel country east of the old frontier: Brandenburg, Sachsen-Anhalt east of the Elbe and Sachsen, the Billung and Gero marches

ledger.note: 936-937: Otto sets up the Billung and Gero marches on the Slav frontier. 'In 936, Otto appointed Hermann Billung as Margrave'; Gero succeeded his brother Siegfried in 937 as margrave of the border region around Merseburg (Otto I page). The land drawn is Cliopatria's 936 growth (Brandenburg, Sachsen-Anhalt, Sachsen), which almost no Cliopatria polity held in 935 (8 of the 221 cells).

region.text: Lotharingia, held by the rebel Duke Gilbert

ledger.note: 939: Otto invades Lotharingia against the rebel Duke Gilbert, who had tried on Henry's death to swap Lotharingia to the West Franks. 'invaded Lotharingia, and at the Battle of Andernach defeated Gilbert, who drowned trying to flee across the Rhine' (Lotharingia page).

region.text: Lotharingia

ledger.note: 939: the revolt of the dukes ends at Andernach. 'Eberhard was killed in battle, and Gilbert drowned in the Rhine while attempting to escape'; 'Otto made peace with Louis IV, whereby Louis recognized his suzerainty over Lorraine' (Otto I page). Otto then ruled Franconia directly.

region.text: the Obotrite country: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and east Holstein, taken from Cliopatria's 947 growth

ledger.note: 947: the Obotrites, whose Cliopatria row ends in 946, appear under the German king in Cliopatria's shape. The page is silent on a date: it has Hermann Billung fighting 'the Lutici, Obotrites, and Wagri' without a year and the Obotrites invading Saxony in fall 955, which is why the land is drawn as tributary rather than annexed.

region.text: the east Elbe and Oder lands of Gero's march (Brandenburg, Sachsen, the Oder), 947 growth without the Obotrite share

ledger.note: 947: Cliopatria's shape grows over the rest of the Elbe-Oder country, Gero's march; no opened page dates it. 'In 941, Gero initiated another plot to subdue the Slavs'; after his death on 20 May 965 'his march was split into five smaller marches' stretching 'from the Billung March in the north to the Duchy of Bohemia in the south' (Otto I page).

region.text: Bohemia

ledger.note: 950: the Bohemian war ends. 'The war was not concluded until 950, when Otto besieged a castle owned by Boleslaus' son' (Otto I page).

region.text: the Duchy of Bohemia

ledger.note: 950: Boleslaus I of Bohemia makes peace and resumes paying tribute to Otto. The page says Boleslaus 'agreed to a peace treaty and to resume paying tribute' and dates the end of the war to 950, but gives no year for the terms themselves (Otto I page).

region.text: Berengar II's kingdom, entered at Pavia

ledger.note: 951: Otto enters Pavia and takes the Lombard crown. 'When Otto arrived at Pavia on 23 September 951, the city willingly opened its gate'; Berengar II 'fled from his capital in Pavia'; Otto used the titles Rex Italicorum and Rex Langobardorum from 10 October (Otto I page).

region.text: Berengar II's kingdom

ledger.note: 952: Otto gives Italy back to Berengar as a fief. 'Appearing before the Diet in August 952 in Augsburg' Berengar II and his son Adalbert swore fealty as Otto's vassals and Berengar kept the Italian kingship as a fief (Otto I page).

minus.text: the March of Verona: the Duchy of Friuli reorganised under Henry of Bavaria, with Verona

region.text: the kingdom of Italy without Friuli and Verona

ledger.note: 952: Berengar II becomes Otto's vassal for the kingdom of Italy. He and his son swore fealty at the Diet of Augsburg in August 952, kept the kingship as a fief and had to pay 'a large annual tribute' (Otto I page).

region.text: the March of Verona: the Duchy of Friuli reorganised under Henry of Bavaria, with Verona

ledger.note: 952: Friuli passes to Otto's brother Henry of Bavaria as the March of Verona. Berengar had to 'cede the Duchy of Friuli'; 'Friuli was reorganized as the March of Verona and placed under Henry's control' (Otto I page); the March 'was annexed by Duchy of Bavaria in 952' (Kingdom of Germany page). Region: Friuli plus a circle at Verona, the researcher's reading of 'March of Verona'.

region.text: the Obotrite country

ledger.note: 955: the Obotrites invade Saxony. 'The Obotrites invaded Saxony in the fall of 955' (Otto I page).

region.text: the Obotrite country

ledger.note: 955: Otto wins at the Recknitz. 'Otto's forces gained a decisive victory' at the Battle of Recknitz on 16 October 955 (Otto I page). The page gives no terms.

region.text: the eastern Alpine and Pannonian lands: Austria, Carinthia, Slovenia

ledger.note: 960: Cliopatria's shape grows over Austria, Slovenia and Carinthia, taken from its Principality of Hungary of 955. The page is silent: it dates the Lechfeld victory (10 August 955) and the March of Verona (952) but describes no eastern march.

region.text: the kingdom of Italy

ledger.note: 961: Otto takes Italy into his own hand. 'Otto's army descended into northern Italy in August 961 through the Brenner Pass'; Berengar's armies avoided battle; Otto assumed the title King of Italy at Pavia around Christmas (Otto I page). Berengar surrendered at San Leo in 963.

region.text: the kingdom of Italy

ledger.note: 961: Otto I becomes King of Italy at Pavia at Christmas, and Cliopatria draws Italy as German for the year. 'Otto assumed the title King of Italy at Pavia around Christmas' (Otto I page).

region.text: the German kingdom and Italy of Otto I

ledger.note: 962: Otto I is crowned Emperor at Rome and the German kingdom becomes the core of the Holy Roman Empire. 'Otto reached Rome on 31 January 962; three days later, he was crowned Emperor' by Pope John XII; 'From 962, the kings of Germany claimed the imperial title' (Kingdom of Germany page).

wars.name: Henry the Fowler's war with Arnulf of Bavaria
wars.outcome: Henry defeated Arnulf in two campaigns in 921 and Arnulf renounced the crown and submitted.
wars.note: The East Francia page says Conrad I's struggle with Arnulf cost him his life; the Kingdom of Germany page quotes an entry of the Annales Iuvavenses of 919 about him.

wars.name: Henry the Fowler's conquest of Lotharingia
wars.outcome: Henry invaded in 923 and the Lotharingians elected him king in 925; Lotharingia became the Duchy of Lorraine within the German kingdom.
wars.note: The Henry the Fowler page adds that Henry met Charles the Simple on 7 November 921 (Treaty of Bonn) and besieged the rebel Duke Gilbert in 925.

wars.name: Henry the Fowler's Slav campaigns
wars.outcome: Henry took Brandenburg (winter 928) and Gana (Jahna) and forced Wenceslaus of Bohemia back to tribute in 929; the Redarii were routed at Lenzen on 4 September 929.

wars.name: Hungarian invasions under Henry the Fowler
wars.outcome: A ten-year truce in 924, then victory at the Battle of Riade in 933, which 'ended Magyar attacks for the next 21 years'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The page dates the truce to 924 where other accounts say 926.

wars.name: Henry the Fowler's Danish campaign
wars.note: The page gives no extent and no later date for the Mark.

wars.name: Otto I's Bohemian war
wars.outcome: Boleslaus I of Bohemia attacked an ally of the Saxons in 936; the war 'was not concluded until 950, when Otto besieged a castle owned by Boleslaus' son', and Boleslaus agreed to peace and to resume paying tribute.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the terms; ledger events use 936 and 950.

wars.name: Revolt of the dukes (Eberhard and Gilbert)
wars.outcome: Eberhard was killed and Gilbert drowned in the Rhine at Andernach in 939; Otto took Franconia into direct rule and Louis IV recognised his suzerainty over Lorraine.
wars.note: Arnulf of Bavaria died in 937 and Berthold replaced his son Eberhard in 938. The Lotharingia page adds that Gilbert rebelled on Henry's death in 936 and that Conrad became duke in 944.

wars.name: Otto I's Italian expedition of 951-952
wars.outcome: Otto entered Pavia on 23 September 951 and took the Lombard crown; Berengar II did homage at Augsburg in August 952, kept Italy as a fief and ceded Friuli, which became the March of Verona.

wars.name: Revolt of Liudolf and Conrad
wars.outcome: The rebellion ended at the Diet of Arnstadt in December 954; Henry was confirmed as Duke of Bavaria.

wars.name: Battle of Lechfeld and the Recknitz campaign
wars.outcome: Otto defeated the Hungarians at the Lechfeld on 10 August 955 and the Obotrites at the Recknitz on 16 October 955.
wars.note: The Lechfeld ended 'nearly 100 years of Hungarian invasions'; the page names no border change.

wars.name: Otto I's Italian expedition of 961-962
wars.outcome: Otto entered Italy in August 961, took the kingship at Pavia around Christmas and was crowned Emperor in Rome in early February 962; Berengar II surrendered at San Leo in 963.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any frontier; the pages opened give no treaty line (the 921 Treaty of Bonn with Charles the Simple is mentioned without one). Frontier marches and tributary zones (Bohemia, the Obotrites, Italy 952-961) are approximate throughout, and the Lotharingian border changes of 925 and 939 are known only as 'Lotharingia'.

notes: Kingdom of Germany (Cliopatria 911..961): one state with East Francia (843) and the later Holy Roman Empire; Cliopatria cuts it at 911 and 962. Dossier ends 3 February 962 at the imperial coronation (the Empire row starts 962, so 962 is drawn twice unless the renderer lets the Empire win). Page budget: 5 pages for this state (Kingdom of Germany, Henry the Fowler, Otto I, East Francia, Lotharingia) plus the Rudolph II of Burgundy page opened for Arles; none of them gives an area, so no infobox comparison was possible. Verified from the pages: 911 election, 919, 921, 923-925 Lotharingia, 926 Basel, 928-929 Slavs, 929 Bohemia, 934 Schleswig, 936 marches, 939 Andernach, 951-952 and 961-962 Italy, 955, 962. Not settled: (1) whether Bavaria and Franconia counted as full territory 911-921; (2) the extent and end of the Mark of Schleswig (loss 936 is confidence 1); (3) the Obotrite and Elbe-Oder land 947 (no page dates it; vassal reading); (4) the eastern Alpine and Pannonian growth of 960 (principality-of-hungary lost it in Cliopatria; no page); (5) 937 Burgundy: Otto backed Conrad of Burgundy against Hugh of Italy, see kingdom-of-arles. Gazetteer names needed: place Brandenburg an der Havel (used for the Hevelli country). Counterparts without a dossier: Hevelli, Gana, the Bavarian duke Arnulf, Gilbert of Lotharingia (a rebel, not a held state for a year), the Redarii. Cliopatria rows seen to be mislabelled for this state: none; the 936 growth is on nobody's land in Cliopatria, the 947 Obotrite land is Obotrites 793..946. | fx-32 F207: the 911-925 shapes were checked against the gazetteer's Lotharingia region: the 177 shared cells are Westphalia east of the Rhine and Worms-Speyer-Koblenz, not Lotharingia proper (Cologne, Aachen, Trier, Metz, the Low Countries are outside the shapes), so no subtraction is made here; the duchy-of-lotharingia keyframe was cut instead.
